original_idea.body:
# Cosmetic-Comment Attacks on Legibility Protocols

**Problem:** Risk: legibility protocols backfire by giving the attacker a new channel. The under-studied link is whether well-written but subtly misleading comments REDUCE a monitor's suspicion of genuinely backdoored code.

**Direction:** Take backdoored code snippets and produce three comment variants: none, honest, and plausibly-misleading. Run an open monitor and measure suspicion score per variant. Test whether misleading comments significantly lower detection.

**Why it matters:** Legibility protocols are a recent improvement, but encouraging more text hands the model a deception channel. Directly stress-tests a published defense. API/open-model feasible.

**Relevant context:** Basic Legibility Protocols (arXiv:2602.10153); CoT Red-Handed (arXiv:2505.23575).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain with explicit links: weaponized comments would reverse a recent legibility-protocol safety gain.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Three comment variants plus monitor scoring; inference-only, beginner-feasible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: suspicion-score drop from misleading vs no comments.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: API/open-model, no lab resources; stress-tests a published defense labs underweight externally.

novelty.reasoning: Legibility protocols very recent; cosmetic-comment attack on them plausibly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Legibility protocol recent; this attack angle plausibly open.
